property_summary: MinSum value as read from the contract equals the value previously passed to SetMinSum
MinSum can never increase once the contract is initialized
MinSum equals the _val passed to SetMinSum before initialization, not its double.
MinSum can never be zero when SetMinSum succeeds with _val equal to 1.
If no call sets MinSum, it remains zero.
SetMinSum always succeeds and cannot revert when the contract has not been initialized
After SetMinSum is called with any value, MinSum must equal that value; the mutant always sets it to 100, violating the rule for any other input.
After a successful SetMinSum call (not reverted), MinSum should equal the passed argument; the buggy version leaves it at default zero, violating the rule.
After initialization and a call to SetMinSum with any value, MinSum must equal that value; the buggy version leaves MinSum at zero, violating the invariant.

For any non-zero amount, if SetMinSum is called with that amount after initialization, then MinSum must equal that amount; the buggy version leaves MinSum at zero, violating the rule for any non-zero input.
After initialization and a successful call to SetMinSum with an argument, MinSum must equal that argument; the buggy version leaves MinSum at zero, violating the rule.

After a successful (non-reverting) call to SetMinSum(x) following initialization, calling Collect with amount x and sufficient balance should not revert; the reference correctly allows it, but the buggy version leaves MinSum at 0, causing a revert.
MinSum must equal the last value passed to SetMinSum; the buggy version adds values, so after two SetMinSum calls it exceeds the last argument.
Setting the log file fails (reverts) even on an uninitialized contract because the condition is permanently true.
SetLogFile reverts when the contract is initialized but not when it is not initialized, which holds for P and is broken by M.

property_summary: SetLogFile always succeeds when called before initialization, regardless of the argument.
The address of the LogFile contract, once initialized, must never change; the bug allows changing LogFile after initialization.
The address of the LogFile contract, once initialized, must remain unchanged; the bug allows changing LogFile after initialization by calling SetLogFile again.
After initialization, the LogFile address must be immutable; the bug allows SetLogFile to overwrite it after initialization.
After initialization, the LogFile address cannot be changed via SetLogFile; the bug allows SetLogFile to reassign LogFile even after initialization.
After the contract is initialized, calling SetLogFile must not change the LogFile address that was set during initialization; the bug allows SetLogFile to overwrite LogFile after initialization.
After calling SetLogFile with a valid address, the LogFile state variable must reference that address; the mutant leaves it uninitialized (zero-address), breaking this invariant.

After calling SetLogFile with any address, the LogFile contract returned by the auto-generated getter must be callable without reverting; the buggy version leaves LogFile as the zero-address, so any external call to it will revert.

After SetLogFile is called with any non-zero address and the contract is initialized, an external low-level call to the LogFile getter's address with the History(uint256) signature using the returned address must succeed and not revert; the bug sets LogFile to zero address, causing the call to revert.

After calling SetLogFile with any address, a subsequent low-level call to the address returned by the LogFile() getter should succeed (not revert), because it is expected to hold a live Log contract; the mutant leaves LogFile unset so the call reverts.

After successful initialization and setting a LogFile, any call to the contract's payable fallback or Put function must not revert; the buggy version incorrectly leaves LogFile unset, causing an external call to the zero-address during Put, which makes any payment attempt revert.
The sum of all Acc balances equals the contract's Ether balance in the reference contract; the buggy contract violates this invariant because Put does not increase the holder's recorded balance.

The contract's Ether balance should be at least the sum of all account balances recorded in Acc; the buggy mutant fails to increment the balance in Put, so a holder's balance lags behind the Ether sent, breaking the invariant that the contract holds enough to cover all recorded claims.

After any number of Puts, a holder's Acc balance must equal the total Ether they have sent to the contract; the buggy mutant fails to update Acc balance, so the recorded balance is less than the actual contributions.
For any user, after calling Put with a lock time and sending msg.value, the user's Acc.balance increases by msg.value; the mutant omits the balance increase, so the balance stays unchanged.

After any sequence of calls to Put, a holder's Acc.balance must equal the total Ether they sent via Put plus any initial balance; the mutant fails to increment the balance, so a holder's recorded balance is less than the sum of their contributions.

After any sequence of Put calls by any address, the stored balance of that address in Acc must equal the total msg.value sent by that address; the mutant breaks this because it adds an extra 1 on each Put call.

After a Put call, the balance stored for a user must equal msg.value plus the pre-existing balance; the mutant increases it by one extra, so total stored balance across all users exceeds the sum of msg.value sent plus initial zero.

After a Put call, the contract's ETH balance equals the sum of all msg.value sent minus any collected amounts, but the mutant creates a mismatch because it stores balance+1 per Put while only receiving msg.value, so sum(Acc balances) will eventually exceed address(c).balance + total collected.

For any address that only ever calls Put (never Collect), its Acc balance must equal the sum of msg.value sent via Put plus any initial balance; the bug adds an extra 1 per Put, so after at least one Put the balance exceeds the total msg.value sent.

For any address, the contract's ETH balance equals the sum of all Acc balances minus the total of 1 per Put call made by that address; the mutant violates this because it adds an extra 1 per Put, breaking the invariant relationship between stored balances and actual ETH held.
After any call to Put, the Log contract's History length must increase (i.e., a new entry was added); the buggy version fails to record the Put so the history length stays the same.
